items.action: Apply the map to every static `variant="…"`. For a dynamic `[variant]="expr"`: if the expression only ever yields hues (primary/error/success/warning), rebind it to `[color]="expr"` verbatim; if it yields a mix of hues and fills, retype it and split it across the two inputs.
items.appliesWhen: `variant="text"` keeps working and its map entry is an identity, so leave it. It warns in dev builds (prefer the global `.link` class) but needs no migration.
items.pitfall: A dynamic `[variant]` left bound to a hue does not fail — the value is simply not a variant any more, so it falls back to `solid` and the button quietly renders in the default colour. Nothing throws and nothing logs in production; only looking at the screen finds it.
items.note: One conflated input became two orthogonal axes: `color` (primary|secondary|tertiary|neutral|error|success|warning, default primary) and `variant` (solid|tonal|ghost|outline|text, default solid).
items.verify: No ds-button carries a variant value outside the shipped set, and every button that used to name a colour through `variant` now names it through the colour input. Buttons render in the colour they did before the upgrade, not all in the default.

items.action: Apply the map in templates, and remap the same literals in TypeScript: the exported `ButtonSize` narrowed from `s|m|l|sm|md|lg` to `sm|md|lg`, so a field or input typed with it and assigned `'s'`, `'m'` or `'l'` stops compiling.
items.appliesWhen: `sm`, `md` and `lg` are unchanged and absent from the map — leave them. A button with no `size` keeps the 40px it had as the old default `l`.
items.pitfall: `m`→`sm` and `l`→`md` are pure renames, but `s`→`sm` is not: the 24px tier is gone and `sm` is 32px, so those buttons get **8px taller** and the row around them reflows. It compiles, it looks deliberate, and only a screen shows it.
items.note: ButtonSize collapsed to sm|md|lg (32/40/48px at default density) and the duplicate one-letter tier was dropped.
items.restore: nothing to restore - the 24px tier is gone; its callers take sm (32px), and an attribute-less button keeps the same 40px it had as `l`
items.verify: No ds-button binds size="s", "m" or "l". A button left without size renders at the md height (40px), and every button that previously said "l" now says "md" and is unchanged on screen.

items.action: Retype per axis. A union of only hues becomes `ButtonColor` and its bindings move to `[color]`; a union of only fills keeps `ButtonVariant` and remaps its values (secondary→tonal, tertiary→ghost, outline stays); a union carrying both must be split into two.
items.pitfall: A mixed union is the one that does not announce itself: it still satisfies neither type cleanly, and the tempting fix — widening it back to `string` — compiles everywhere and moves the failure to runtime, where an unknown value silently falls back to the default.
items.note: `ButtonVariant` now holds the fill vocabulary (solid|tonal|ghost|outline|text); the hues moved to a new exported `ButtonColor` (primary|secondary|tertiary|neutral|error|success|warning).
items.verify: Nothing types a hue with ButtonVariant: the fill vocabulary and the hue live in two unions now, and a field or method feeding [variant] carries the fill one.

items.action: Wrap every group of `<ds-radio value>` that is bound into a reactive or template-driven form in `<ds-radio-group>`, and move `formControlName` / `[formControl]` / `[(ngModel)]` onto the group.
items.appliesWhen: A standalone `<ds-radio [(checked)]>` outside a form is unaffected.
items.note: `ds-radio-group` is the container and the form control now: it owns the ControlValueAccessor, the roving tabindex, the `name`, and the group label, invalid and hint.
items.verify: Every radio group bound into a form sits inside a ds-radio-group that owns the control, the name and the roving tabindex.

items.note: Helper and error text is rendered by the shared `ds-field-message` now, so the hook reaches every field's message line rather than only the input's.

items.action: Read every `(closed)` handler and check it does not depend on running in the same tick as the click.
items.pitfall: The handlers that break are the ones that look harmless: re-opening the sheet immediately now races the leave animation, and a focus move made in the handler lands while the panel is still on screen and gets taken back.
items.note: The close animates, so `(closed)` emits at the END of the leave animation instead of on the click.
items.verify: No (closed) handler assumes it fires synchronously on the click - an immediate re-open or a focus move now lands after the leave animation.

items.action: None, unless you relied on the pressed halo. To keep it, declare `--ds-button-pressed-shadow` explicitly.
items.appliesWhen: Only where the token was being read. No usage, no action.
items.note: The faint pressed halo now defaults to `none`; press feedback is a darken plus a micro scale-down.
items.verify: Nothing relied on the pressed halo; a screen that wants it sets the token.

items.action: Look at the disabled state of every button variant you actually use. To go back to the flat grey, pin the per-variant `--ds-button-*-disabled` / `--ds-icon-button-*-disabled` hooks.
items.pitfall: The tint is derived from each variant's own colour, so a brand that recoloured one variant gets a disabled state it never chose — and because nothing in the API moved, no build or type check points at it.
items.note: Disabled is a per-variant muted tint now rather than one flat grey: solid and text take a flat pale oklch tint, while tonal, ghost, outline and the icon-button tonal and outlined variants use `color-mix` with `--surface-disabled`.
items.restore: the per-variant disabled colour hooks pinned to the old flat values
items.verify: The disabled state of every variant in use was looked at once - it derives from the variant's own colour now rather than one shared grey.

items.action: Read every close-related handler on `ds-modal` and `ds-drawer` and check it does not depend on running in the same tick as the dismiss.
items.pitfall: Same shape as the bottom sheet: an immediate re-open races the leave animation, and a focus hand-off made in the handler lands while the panel is still visible.
items.note: Both animate their close now — animate-then-remove, like ds-bottom-sheet — and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, so close-related outputs fire at the end of the leave animation.
items.verify: No teardown or focus move assumes the dismiss is synchronous: close-related outputs fire at the END of the leave animation.

items.action: Add the `@use` beside your existing `styles/tokens` import.
items.appliesWhen: Only if you import `styles/tokens` a la carte. The `styles/ds` entry forwards both, so its users need nothing.
items.note: The `--bp-*` custom properties moved into a new `styles/breakpoints` partial, so a tokens-only importer no longer gets them.

informational: Many new components (multi-select, slider, otp-input, color-picker, tree, segmented, button-group, split-button, toggle-button, list, timeline, description-list, stack/inline/container, loading-overlay, radio-group, alert) — additive.

ds-color scoped-accent system (--accent-* pointer layer, [ds-color] attribute, ds.color() mixin) + dark theme (opt-in via data-theme=dark, provideDsTheme({followSystem})) — additive, light output unchanged.

Reactive-forms (CVA) + invalid/hint on checkbox, switch, combobox, date-picker; hint/invalid on select; inline [label] on checkbox/radio/switch; input [loading]/[floating]; --field-label-gap — additive.

ds-button overlay-trigger inputs (ariaHasPopup/ariaExpanded/buttonRef); date-picker month/year grid pickers; table pagination/clientSort/stickyFirstColumn; ModalService.confirm(); dropzone per-file message + queued state — additive.
$bp-* Sass breakpoint aliases + up()/down() mixins; new disabled-state and press-scale override tokens — additive (a-la-carte styles/tokens importers also need styles/breakpoints now).

Visual-only: button/icon-button press is darken + micro scale-down; [disabled] is a per-variant muted tint (override --ds-*-disabled tokens to restore flat grey); smooth motion pass across components; reduced-motion no longer freezes spinners; overlay scroll-lock release fix.

A collapsed ds-accordion item now collapses to nothing, where its padding stayed behind on the clipped wrapper and left a strip of empty height; the padding is restored when the item expands. If you zeroed that padding to hide the strip, the item will now be flat when open. NO ACTION otherwise.
